note: PRE reproduced and frozen BEFORE any edit, on the exact branch the order names: the final witness 'done' write reaches modeled storage, its fsync fails, the restoration also fails. Same-process visibility never counted as persistence.

ack_final_witness.verdict: recovery depended on WHICH un-guaranteed bytes happened to land: the done-reached branch authorized the transition the caller was told is uncertain, contradicting E13's own claim that every crash branch fails closed.

route_lock_final_witness.branch_released_and_done_reached_storage: ENTERED and registered over the rejected release

run_lock_final_witness.branch_released_and_done_reached_storage: ENTERED over the release the caller saw fail

PRE.contract_defect: the model assumed an fsync error proves the preceding bytes did not persist; completion was an OVERWRITE of the durable intent; nothing bound a completion to its generation.

POST.design: append-only. An immutable, generation-bound intent record is durable BEFORE the transition; success is a SEPARATE exclusive self-integral completion record persisted only after all protected data is durable; nothing is overwritten or deleted to establish success; NO restoration write exists or is trusted (asserted at source level). Recovery evaluates the PHYSICAL state.

receipt_acknowledgement.intent: <seq>.json.aw — sealed JSON {schema, route, seq, generation, record_digest}, written once
receipt_acknowledgement.completion: <seq>.json.done — same fields, same generation, exclusive create after the digest acknowledgement is durable
receipt_acknowledgement.branch_completion_fully_reached_storage: recovered COMPLETED — idempotent accept of the physically complete record, though the caller was told uncertain
receipt_acknowledgement.stale_generation: a completion naming another generation refuses; a completion transplanted from another sequence refuses

locks.content: held:<pid>:<epoch> -> releasing:<epoch> -> released:<epoch>, in place, never unlinked
locks.records: rel.<epoch> intent durable before the lock moves; reldone.<epoch> completion only after released is durable
locks.entry_rule: a claimant enters ONLY over released:<epoch> whose epoch-bound completion verifies, revalidated descriptor-first under the reclaim election
locks.branch_completion_reached_storage: claimant ENTERS — the release physically completed (route lock: next registration proceeds; run lock: completed plan resumes)
locks.branch_released_reached_storage_no_compl: REFUSED for both locks — the PRE counterexamples die
locks.bare_unepoched_released: refused: not a completed epoch release
locks.stale_epoch_completion: refused: a stale completion never releases a new holder

POST.boundary_map: seven directory-fsync boundaries: 1 route-dir=clean, 2 lock-acquire=lock_held, 3 intent=uncertain, 4 post-rename=uncertain, 5 completion=COMPLETE (the physically complete record stands, next sequence registers), 6 release-intent=lock_held, 7 release-completion=clean — each read by a FRESH process
POST.contention: two REAL processes over the recovered-complete state: at least one idempotently accepts, none double-registers; two real processes over an uncertain route and over an uncompleted release: all fail closed
POST.descriptor_checks: E13's no-follow, owner, regular-file and 0600 checks preserved and extended to completion records (symlink and wrong-mode parametrizations include .json.done)

self_reported_notes: my first PRE probe for the acknowledgement failed the INTENT-phase fsync instead of the final witness write and raised a raw OSError without reproducing; the arming was corrected (fail only the final 'done', then the restoration) and the PRE then reproduced all three findings exactly.

lock content now carries its epoch, so four accepted-battery assertions that compared the literal string 'released' were updated to released:<epoch> plus completion checks — behaviours preserved, format evolved with the protocol; disclosed rather than silently rewritten.

the two-process uncertain-route contention keeps its E13 finding: the claimant that loses the lock race refuses on the held lock rather than classifying the route — both outcomes fail closed and the assertion states exactly that.
boundaries: C7-C10 and E1-E13 behaviours preserved. Final durability model scope only: no venue connection, no services, no commands, no position changes, no WP4 dispatch, no training. Per the order's gate, E14 acceptance would close effect-free WP3 and may unlock WP4 implementation/materialization and benchmarks only — live activation and all venue effects remain separately blocked. That acceptance is Musashi's, not mine.
